title: Cloud SQL Connection Limits

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.3.35 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.3.35 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`google:gcp:monitoring` collected via `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:monitoring" metric.type="cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/network/connections"
| table _time resource.type metric.type value
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.35_cloud_sql_connection_lim_35"
| sort -_time
description: Hitting max connections causes application errors; trending connections versus tier limits guides pool sizing and read replicas.
value: Detecting cloud sql connection limits early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Maintain lookup of instance tier to max connections. Alert at 85% sustained. Correlate with connection pool metrics from apps. Plan vertical scale or read replicas before hard failures.
visualization: Line chart (connections vs limit), Gauge (utilization %), Table (instance, conns).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `google:gcp:monitoring`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `resource.type` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Maintain lookup of instance tier to max connections. Alert at 85% sustained. Correlate with connection pool metrics from apps. Plan vertical scale or read replicas before hard failures.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:monitoring" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:monitoring" metric.type="cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/network/connections"
| table _time resource.type metric.type value
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.35_cloud_sql_connection_lim_35"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:monitoring` in `index=gcp` to detect cloud sql connection limits. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `resource.type` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_35_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (connections vs limit), Gauge (utilization %), Table (instance, conns)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud sql connection limits so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
